observable_outcome: An error that must not be shown to a caller is written where the operator can read it, and nowhere else. Measured at 0433758: domainError's unclassified branch (internal/api/api.go:1256-1261) answers 500 internal_error with the constant "internal server error" and deliberately drops the err value on the floor; ServeHTTP's recover branch (api.go:49-53) reads `if recover() != nil` and discards the recovered value without binding it; and ZERO non-test files under internal/ or cmd/ import "log" or "log/slog", so neither text exists anywhere in the process afterwards. This task gives both branches one destination: a single-line JSON record on the process's stdout, which Cloud Run hands to Cloud Logging and preview-local puts in the owner's own terminal. The record carries the correlation id, the method, the path and the error's own text; the RESPONSE gains nothing -- still exactly the four keys error, message, schema_version, correlation_id with the same constant message, and the same X-Correlation-ID header. Nothing is written to Firestore, because the fault being recorded is usually a Firestore fault and because a caller-provokable write would drain the daily write budget that domainError's own 429 branch guards. The record is bounded by a closed struct with no free-form field, a 256-byte cap on the text and on the path, and a 32-records-per-minute cap whose dropped lines are announced by a marker and counted exactly on the next line. Time comes only from an injected clock. No route is added; the operator is told where to look in the GCP runbook.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written into all three evidence records BEFORE any source file is edited, as a table with one row each. (2) What it deliberately does not do: it changes no response body by one byte, no status code, no error's Error() text, no stored field, no contract document, no route and no request or response field; it writes nothing to Firestore; it adds no environment variable and no configuration knob; and it reads no request body, no header and no query string. (3) What it records but does not fix: that docs/operations/gcp-runbook.md said nothing at all about reading logs before this task (re-measure); that internal/api/live_local_test.go starts the binary through runner.ProcessSupervisor with Stdout nil (live_local_test.go:159 at 0433758) so records appear in that test's -v output but cannot be asserted there because the file is prohibited; and that internal/provider's ForbiddenPatternMatches/SecretPatternMatches are used only from the test, because a source import would demand a ci/components.json edit. (4) What only a later task can establish: that the record is readable in real Cloud Logging on a real Cloud Run revision -- that is V2-014/V2-054's GCP grade, not this task's, and this task must not claim it. (5) That this task passes no release gate on its own.

Record all four measurements yourself: (a) `grep -rn '"log"\|"log/slog"' --include=*.go internal cmd | grep -v _test.go` returns nothing, so this repository still has no logging idiom; (b) domainError's unclassified branch passes a constant and never err.Error(), so the err value is dropped (cite the measured line numbers); (c) ServeHTTP's recover branch does not even bind the recovered value; (d) ci/components.json declares api's dependencies as application, domain, infra, runner, web and api's verification_dependencies as control-plane, provider, release, store-firestore, store-memory, update. If (a) is no longer true -- if some other task added a logger first -- STOP and escalate rather than adding a second mechanism.

A4. The recorder, as a closed type in a new file internal/api/operator_record.go. Declare: an exported port `OperatorRecorder` with one method taking one struct value; an exported observation struct carrying exactly the four inputs a call site may supply (correlation id, method, path, detail) plus the kind; an exported `JSONOperatorRecorder`; and the constructor `NewJSONOperatorRecorder(w io.Writer, clock application.Clock) (*JSONOperatorRecorder, error)` which returns an error for a nil writer and for a nil clock. The emitted line is a closed struct with json tags and NO map and NO free-form field, whose keys are exactly: schema_version ("v1"), kind, severity ("ERROR"), observed_at, correlation_id, method, path, status, error, detail, detail_truncated, suppressed_before, and window_seconds plus records_per_window only on the suppression marker. kind is one of exactly three values: unclassified_error, recovered_panic, suppression_started. detail and path each pass through runner.RedactLog and are then capped at 256 bytes with detail_truncated recording the fact. The recorder holds a sync.Mutex, a window start and two counters; it must contain no goroutine, no timer, no time.Now call and no source of randomness.

A5. The recorder is proved ALONE, with no HTTP involved, in a new file internal/api/operator_record_test.go (package api_test). Assert by equality on the emitted bytes, using a bytes.Buffer sink and the existing steppable framingClock (api_test.go:3138 at 0433758) so every line is deterministic: (a) one observation produces exactly one line, and the line equals the expected JSON byte for byte; (b) the key set, obtained by unmarshalling into map[string]any, is EXACTLY the declared set -- the same technique V2-083 used for the four response keys -- so a field cannot be added unnoticed; (c) redaction: a bearer token, a PEM private-key header and a gh token placed in the detail AND in the path each come out as [REDACTED], and `runner.RedactLog(line) == line` (idempotence) holds for the emitted line; (d) truncation: a detail longer than 256 bytes is cut to 256 with detail_truncated true, and a path longer than 256 the same way; (e) bounding: 200 observations inside one window produce exactly 33 lines -- 32 records then one suppression_started marker naming window_seconds and records_per_window -- and after the clock is stepped past the window the next line carries suppressed_before equal to the exact number dropped and then resets to 0; (f) the constructor refuses a nil writer and a nil clock. Build every secret-shaped fixture by concatenating a prefix with a suffix so the pattern exists at run time and not in the file.
